title: Dependent Choice and the Complete-Metric Baire Theorem

items.title: The serial-relation Dependent Choice principle over ZF
items.statement: Over ZF, DC says: for every NONEMPTY set A and R subset A x A with (forall a in A)(exists b in A) a R b, there is f:omega->A with f(n) R f(n+1) for all n. Also state the prescribed-start variant for each a0 in A. Serial means successors exist, with the displayed direction. No distinctness, transitivity or irreflexivity is required.

items.title: Prescribed-start and starting-point-free serial choice are equivalent in ZF
items.statement: ZF equivalence of the two global principles. For the nontrivial direction fix a0 and let P be the set of tagged nonempty finite R-paths starting at a0. Successor relation is one-step end extension. P is nonempty and serial using only one existential successor at a time. Starting-point-free DC on P yields paths p_k whose lengths are length(p_0)+k, nested and unbounded. Their union is a function on omega starting at a0 and following R. The arbitrary first path already contains the prescribed start. Finite-path set existence: Separation in omega x P(omega x A); union is a function by compatibility. No invocation of the old def-dependent-choice or any choice principle besides the antecedent.

items.title: The complete-metric Baire principle over ZF
items.statement: Work in ZF with omega indexed families. In a metric space, N is nowhere dense iff int(cl N) is empty. M is meagre iff there exists a sequence (N_n) of nowhere dense sets with M subset union_n N_n; comeagre means complement meagre. A space is Baire iff every sequence of open dense sets has dense intersection. CM-Baire is the assertion that every complete metric space is Baire, including the vacuous empty-space case. Closure, interior and density are metric notions already supplied. Do not assert that a countable union of unspecified meagre sets is meagre in ZF.

items.title: Open-dense and closed-nowhere-dense Baire forms are equivalent in ZF
items.statement: For each metric space, equivalence of: every omega intersection of open dense sets is dense; every union of an omega sequence of closed nowhere dense sets has empty interior; every nonempty open set is nonmeagre in the ambient space; every comeagre subset is dense. Prove closed F nowhere dense iff X minus F open dense using closure/interior definitions and nonempty open test. Apply indexed De Morgan with nonempty index omega. For a given meagre witness (N_n), replace it by the canonically defined (cl N_n); do not choose a decomposition for each of a family of meagre sets. All complements relative to X.

items.title: Serial Dependent Choice implies the complete-metric Baire principle over ZF
items.statement: Assume DC, a complete metric (X,d), open dense U_n, and nonempty open V. States (n,c,r) have n in omega, c in X, rational 0<r<=1/(n+1), and closed ball C(c,r) subset V intersect U_n. Initial state exists at n=0. Relation advances n to n+1 and requires C(c_new,r_new) subset B(c,r) intersect U_(n+1), with rational positive radius <=1/(n+2). Density gives a centre in the open intersection; an open neighbourhood and a smaller reciprocal radius give the closed-ball inclusion. Apply prescribed-start DC to this set of states. Centres c_n are part of the chosen states; for m>=n, c_m in C(c_n,r_n), so for m,k>=n distances <=2r_n->0. Completeness gives x. Prove x in C(c_n,r_n) directly from d(x,c_n)<=d(x,c_m)+r_n by epsilon contradiction, or prove closedness of metric closed balls from the triangle inequality locally. Hence x in V and every U_n. No general Cantor-intersection or closure-to-sequence theorem is used; those published suppliers require AC_omega. Empty X needs no construction.

items.title: Discrete sequence spaces are complete in ZF
items.statement: For every nonempty A define Y=A^omega (nonempty via a single constant function) and d(f,g)=0 if equal, otherwise 1/(k+1) where k is the least differing coordinate. Verify the ultrametric inequality by agreement of initial segments. For finite s:n->A the cylinder [s] consists of its extensions; [s] is nonempty by a constant tail, clopen, and cylinders form a metric basis. For a Cauchy sequence (f_j) and each n let K_n be the LEAST K such that all p,q>=K have d(f_p,f_q)<1/(n+1). Set f(n)=f_(K_n)(n), a uniquely defined coordinate, so Replacement supplies f without choice. For any finite prefix choose the maximum of finitely many K_n; all later f_j agree with f there. Reciprocal radii prove convergence. Scope is the explicitly metrized constant-factor sequence space above; no general product-completeness or product-nonemptiness theorem is asserted.

items.title: Successor-occurrence sets of a serial relation are open and dense
items.statement: For nonempty A and serial R on A, let Y=A^omega with the preceding metric and U_n={f in Y: exists m in omega, f(n) R f(m)}. This is an omega indexed family of open dense sets. Openness follows from a witnessing m and fixing coordinates through max(n,m). To meet a cylinder [s], extend s to determine coordinate n (use one fixed a_* in A if needed), choose ONE R-successor b of that value, append b at a fresh coordinate m>n outside the prefix, and extend with a_* forever. This proves existence separately for each cylinder and n, not a simultaneous countable selection. No path space assumed nonempty.

items.title: The complete-metric Baire principle implies Dependent Choice over ZF
items.statement: Assume CM-Baire and let R be serial on nonempty A. Y=A^omega is nonempty complete in ZF and intersection of the U_n is dense, hence nonempty. Fix f in this intersection. The function q(i)=min{j in omega: f(i) R f(j)} exists by Separation and least-element theorem; recursion gives k(0)=0,k(n+1)=q(k(n)). Then a_n=f(k(n)) is an R-chain. The index sequence need not be increasing and values need not be distinct. Starting-point-free DC is obtained, and the earlier equivalence yields prescribed-start DC. Alternatively intersect with the cylinder f(0)=a0; do not use that alternative to omit the binding starting-point equivalence.

items.title: Dependent Choice is equivalent to the complete-metric Baire principle over ZF
items.statement: Over ZF, the serial-relation DC principle (equivalently its prescribed-start form) holds iff every complete metric space is Baire. Both directions refer to the precise local definitions. This is an internal equivalence, not a consistency or independence theorem, and no DMC comparison appears.

title: Dependent Choice and the Complete-Metric Baire Theorem — Examples

items.title: Blair's sequence space for a serial relation
items.statement: Use A=omega and i R j iff j=i+1. The complete sequence space has U_n={f: some coordinate equals f(n)+1}. From prefix (2,0,2), demonstrate meeting U_0 by appending 3 at coordinate 3 and then a constant tail. The sequence f=(2,0,2,1,3,4,5,...) belongs to every U_n but is not itself an R-chain (2 R 0 fails). Least-index extraction starting at coordinate 0 yields indices 0,4,5,6,... and values 2,3,4,5,... . Also state for arbitrary serial R that membership in all U_n encodes successor availability in the range, not adjacency. This concrete verification is ZF and uses no independent B supplier.
